refuted_claims:
R1 (owner-facing framing is inverted). Claim, verdict_cn: "同一段文字拿来和自己比，有 14% 到 17% 的概率被判成'有效'"; report 0.1: "13.6%-17.3% in a measured split-half null".
- What I checked: protocol.py (TRIGGER_RUNS = 4 on SearchQA, OfficeQA and LiveMath) and the explorer's own b12_stdout.txt and b12b_stdout.txt.
- What I found: the 13.6-17.3% comes from a split-half with 2 runs per side, no placebo condition and no confirm round. The registered gate never runs in that configuration.
- The explorer's own simulation of the full registered gate gives an identical-text FWER of 0.004-0.008 per step. That is LOWER than v5 without the placebo condition (0.014-0.024) and equal to v5 with it (0.005-0.009). Realized-panel registered C1 for parent:B is 0.007.
- So v5 buys power (0.568 -> 0.637/0.683 for a seed-sized effect) at slightly MORE false-positive risk. The summary tells the owner the reverse.
- The same summary presents the C2' margins (6/10/9/15/25) as protection. Yet v5's 25-point ALFWorld margin lets a 10-point harm pass more often than v3 does (0.63 vs 0.56, the report's own table).

R2 (the standing positive control is broken for the seeded chain). Claim, 4.8 / rec. 6: P = the task-card seed toggled (removed when the parent has it) on a 40-item panel of the parent's train failures, "rejected in 98.0%/100% of resampled panels".
- What I checked: a faithful construction. The pool is the failures of the real v3 I-ds stage-1 train unit: 54 items, 25 of them dead. I measured them in cal-1 with byte-identical SHAs.
- Remove direction, which is the owner's good-instruction baseline: ids-full minus scaffold = -2.78 pt (se 5.52) at 2 runs and -3.24 pt (se 4.90) at 4 runs. Detection at n=40 is 0.001.
- Within cal-1, over all 6 train/gate run splits, detection is 0.00-0.16 for a seed-only parent and 0.00 for an ids-full parent.
- The seed's effect sits outside the seeded parent's failures: +13.76 pt on the other 146 items (38 up / 1 down).
- Add direction with failures selected in another session (v3 E-ds train, 55 items): +8.18 pt, detection 0.24/0.37/0.51 at n=20/30/40, not 0.98-1.00.
- Consequence: as specified, every seeded-parent round would be labelled "insensitive" and all its rejections "undetermined".
- A cheap fix exists. Draw the panel from the seeded parent's train passes (0.965 detection at n=40) or from random items (0.887 at n=80, 0.961 at n=100).

R3 (C1' error control is against the wrong null). Claim: "FWER 0.005-0.024"; risk 7: "only replication across sessions, no-harm and transfer separate it from a useful rule".
- What I checked: exact tests on realized cal-1 panels drawn from the 74-item eligible pool.
- The quoted rate covers only a byte-identical parent copy. The test itself is valid: a zero-mean placebo (control:4) passes at 0.03-0.05 at nominal 0.05, and runs are exchangeable (within-copy disagreement 0.111 vs across-copy 0.102).
- But content-free or net-harmful texts pass often:
  - control:2: 0.12-0.25 at p<=.05 and 0.03-0.11 at p<=.01.
  - cand (net -2.75 pt over 200 items, -10.8 outside the eligible pool): 0.26-0.55 and 0.13-0.35.
  - The "beats placebos" condition barely binds (cand, n=11: 0.237 -> 0.234).
- Replication across sessions does not separate these effects. Per-item text effects persist across rounds (r 0.57-0.61).
- The only rule measured in three sessions is E-ds s1-r1, whose SHA equals cal-1 'cand'. Its pooled screen+confirm exact p was 7.75e-6 (G +1.875). On the same 6 trigger items in cal-1 it gave T=4, p=0.32, G +0.50.
- C1' is fixed-panel inference (Clark 1973, the language-as-fixed-effect fallacy, JVLVB 12:335-359). It does not measure benefit that replicates on new items.

R4 (the version-level 3-point test is infeasible as sized). Claims: "macro NI ... SE_macro ~1.13, harmless pass ~0.84, 20.5M-72M" and "SearchQA 642 items", with the requirement "on items not used to propose".
- What I checked: protocol.py POOLS. SearchQA's whole pool is 600 items, fewer than 642. OfficeQA (74) and ALFWorld (57) focal panels are their entire training pools.
- I reproduced SE_macro = 1.135 from the stated inputs. It uses the full focal panels, so it includes proposed-on items.
- It also reuses the same OfficeQA and ALFWorld items at every step. That is a de facto fixed validation set, which the owner forbids (adaptive reuse: Dwork et al. 2015, Science 349:636).
- Excluding the proposal half raises SE_macro to 1.18-1.36 (harmless pass 0.81-0.71), or 1.61 if every benchmark is halved (harmless pass 0.59).
- No script for the macro numbers exists in the artifacts.

R5 (hidden pre-launch cost). Claim: "periodic full calibration ~5M" and "re-measure per benchmark before freezing".
- With the report's own per-cell costs, a cal-1-type calibration (4 arms x focal panel x 4 runs) on all five benchmarks costs about 41M (scaffold) to 143M (seeded) real tokens.
- ALFWorld alone is 26-106M of that. The ledger can charge about 1.9x real.
- The cost table leaves this out, and it is comparable to the whole 139M v3 run.
confirmed_claims:
All of the following were recomputed with my own code; scripts and stdout are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dulin-Documents-Paper-SkillOpt/e7258b97-b430-4dd5-959d-eb871e7c777f/scratchpad/feas/D8-critic/.

cal-1 data:
- 8,800 cells: 6,008 pass / 2,777 fail / 15 unknown. Pre-round 270/130.
- The frozen old-machine unit.json unknown_runs sum to 15 (2+2+1+3+3+1+3), so the "21 unknown runs" line in cal1-registration-20261020.md is wrong, as the explorer says.
- Every contrast vs parent:A matches: cand -2.75; controls -3.75 / +3.38 / -10.00 / 0.00; parent:B +0.75; ids-full +9.17; seed-only +8.75; seed-rule +0.29; seed-rule3 -3.12.
- Same-text per-item SD is 0.139 at 4 runs, with 36 discordant items.
- 74 eligible items; 25 dead items, all inside the eligible pool. The eligible vs other split matches (cand +10.9 / -10.8, seed-only +20.5 / +1.9).

Pilot:
- Spike: 22/24 target runs vs 8/24 for the parent.
- Non-targets: +5.80 pt [+1.97, +9.63], 39 up / 17 down. +16.54 pt on the 68 eligible non-targets and 0.00 on the 126 others.
- Seed effect +9.50 (se 2.25) vs +8.25 (se 2.12); difference +1.25 (se 1.96).
- Session drift -1.88 (se 1.04).
- The conclusions that the spike is not a known-effect control and that the gate cannot see leakage are sound.

Worked example (s1-r1):
- Exact p: screen 0.00765, confirm 0.00051, pooled 7.75e-6; G +1.75 and +2.00.
- The rest sums reconcile with the frozen -4 and -15/2 once the 8 evidence items are excluded.

Statistical validity:
- Runs are exchangeable within a round, so the hypergeometric null is valid for identical text.

Simulation outputs and arithmetic:
- b12, b12b and b13 match the quoted power and FWER.
- Futility: 10/17 arms stopped, 0 of the 3 C1 passers among them, 15.60M of 27.01M saved. Two caveats: 5.90M of that (38%) is one ALFWorld arm (I-ds s5-r1). On SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld (TRIGGER_RUNS=2), "look 1" is the full trigger measurement, so it is C1-first ordering rather than an interim look.
- Margins 6/10/9/15/25, C3' 9/13/16/14 and delta_min 4.8/5.7/9.0/6.3/10.0 all check out. So do the macro 20.5M / 72M costs and the 63% / 74% ALFWorld shares.

Literature (consistent with web checks):
- Holm controls FWER under any dependence.
- Non-binding futility preserves alpha.
- R mantelhaen.test(exact=TRUE) is the exact conditional test given the stratum margins.
- Freidlin, Korn & Gray 2010, Clinical Trials 7(3):197-208.
- The Wieand 1994 half-information rule.
missing:
Positive control and baseline:
- A positive control that works for seeded parents: a pass-selected or random panel of 80-100 items, measured within a round on every benchmark.
- Operating characteristics for rules ON TOP of the task card (the owner's baseline). No cal-1 arm measures seed+rule vs seed. The seeded parent's failure pool is 54 items, 46% of them dead, so power will be lower than the scaffold-based numbers.

Generalization and transfer:
- Any test of benefit on NEW items. C1' is fixed-panel; C2', C3' and the version-level test are no-harm tests; C4' is demoted to descriptive. Nothing in v5 tests the generalization or similar-benchmark-transfer yardstick, and no transfer test is sized.

Error control:
- A realistic null (content-free text) in the FWER statement.
- A replication requirement on fresh items or a third session, plus a winner's-curse correction of G.
- Chain-level error control. The persistence argument used for FWER applies across steps too, but only per-step error is controlled (about 5 x 0.02 per chain).

Version-level test and budget:
- A version-level test sized inside the real pools (600 / 74 / 283 / 120 / 57) without a reused fixed panel, plus a saved script for it.
- A budget for the pre-freeze calibrations (about 41-143M real tokens).
- A budget for re-runs after control-chart flags: the report's own data flag about 2 of 10 session measurements.

Smaller gaps:
- Phase-2 interleaving of parent, rest and P cells under C1-first dispatch is not specified.
- mid-p or randomized exact tests are not considered (the exact test runs at 0.2-3.1% against nominal 5%).
- delta_min feeds no decision rule.
notes_cn: 复核：主要数字我用原始数据重算后一致，方法本身是标准做法，但有三处必须改。一，摘要说 v3“同一段文字和自己比有 14%–17% 被判有效”，这个数来自只跑 2 次、没有复核轮的简化测试；探索者自己的模拟显示 v3 完整门槛误判约 0.5%，比新方案还低，新方案换来的是更强的检测能力，不是更少误判。二，“说明书开关”这个固定对照在带说明书的那条链上几乎测不出来（40 题检出约 0.1%），因为它只从父版本做错的题里抽题；改从做对的题或随机题里抽即可修复。三，整版本“掉分不超过 3 分”的检验所需题数超过训练池，或者每步都要重复用同一批题，等于固定验证集。
